fields.summary: Review triples in HTTP representations for legitimacy

comments.body: Unknown, I think I am right in assuming that you have removed all JCR-triples from the representations?

Yes and no. The representations themselves are in a pretty good state now. The main exception to that is:

    <> fedora:exportAs </foo/fcr:export?format=jcr/xml>
    </foo/fcr:export?format=jcr/xml> dc:format <http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml>

The other issue is that FedoraResourceImpl::getTriples(), when requesting server managed triples, will include all sorts of internal JCR properties: jcr:primaryType, jcr:mixinTypes, etc, which the HTTP api then filters out after the fact. It would be much better to simply not produce those triples in the first place. I have a ticket to remove those: FCREPO-1935 Closed , but first, we need to change how the template rendering happens, which depends on the existence of those properties. See FCREPO-1934 Closed .

W/R/T the fcr::export endpoint, that seems tied directly to a JCR representation of the internal node. Is that deprecated now? Especially given the camel-based serialization tool? Andrew Woods can weigh in on that.

As a side note, the current F4 ontology contains a number of JCR-specific properties that should be evaluated: frozenMixinTypes, frozenPrimaryTypes, frozenUuid, hasNodeType, mixinTypes, primaryType, uuid, UnmappedType, hasDefaultWorkspace, hasWorkspace, hasWorkspaces. There may be others in this category, but those jumped out at me.
I'll open a separate ticket for bad properties in the ontology.

I have no problem with the JCR/XML export format. It's not a part of our ontology, it's just one possible format amongst whatever. Unless we dislike it for other reasons, or just because it exposes impl? Those things aren't good, but the fact that it is part of the triples doesn't bother me. I don't think.

The only issues I have with the export format is that the generated RDF violates the single subject rule (see the RDF snippet above). The RDF also implies that http://fedora.info/definitions/v4/repository#jcr/xml exists in the ontology, which is does not (and should not).

Those are good points. I'm not sure whether we have to maintain the single-subject rule for exports, if export is something other than the result of a GET request. Of course, I would prefer that it just be the result of a GET request.
I just noticed that the RDF from a Binary description still contains some JCR properties, in particular mix:mimeType and nt:resource.
I looked through the various representations of resources (from the current 4.8.0-SNAPSHOT), and I'm in favor of closing this issue. I did not see any MODE- or JCR-related triples.
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing. It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.
